In a particular shop, eggs are sold in cartons. There are $10$ eggs in each carton. The weight of an egg, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $60g$ and a standard deviation of $5g$, while the weight of a carton, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $30g$ and a standard deviation of $2g$. If one carton containing eggs is randomly selected, what is the probability that it weighs less than $653g$? You may assume that the weights are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $0.00$ | $0.01$ | $0.02$ | $0.03$ | $0.04$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $1.2$ | $0.8849$ | $0.8869$ | $0.8888$ | $0.8907$ | $0.8925$ |
| $1.3$ | $0.9032$ | $0.9049$ | $0.9066$ | $0.9082$ | $0.9099$ |
| $1.4$ | $0.9192$ | $0.9207$ | $0.9222$ | $0.9236$ | $0.9251$ |

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.

A math test is composed of $15$ exercises. The time that a student takes to solve an exercise, in minutes, is normally distributed with a mean of $6min$ and a standard deviation of $2min$. If one student is randomly selected, what is the probability that they will take between $80min$ and $100min$ to complete all exercises? You may assume that the times spent solving each exercise are mutually independent.

The time it takes John to get to school, in minutes, is normally distributed with a mean of $20\,\text{min}$ and a standard deviation of $6\,\text{min}.$
What is the probability that the sum of the times John takes to get to school on $5$ randomly selected school days is more than $90\,\text{min}?$
You may assume that the times of each day are mutually independent.
